title: Trout and ricotta dip with roast cherry tomatoes

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole food or a plain dairy staple: trout, ricotta, fresh veg, herbs, lemon and olive oil.

supermarket.reason: Trout fillets, ricotta, cherry tomatoes and the crudité veg are everyday lines at any mainstream supermarket.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a roasting tray, a bowl, a fork and a knife, and the techniques are roasting, flaking and mashing.

works.reason: Two trout fillets mashed into 250g ricotta with 400g roast tomatoes and three vegetables for dipping is a sensible snack for four, and the 200°C timings will cook the fish through without burning the tomatoes.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes is a fair estimate for slicing garlic, zesting, snipping chives, mashing and cutting the veg into sticks, and 25 minutes of cooking matches 10 plus 12 minutes of roasting and a short cool.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item is used in the steps, including the thyme, lemon, chives and the cucumber, radishes and carrots as the 'veg', and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: A light dip with roast cherry tomatoes and crudités suits a June afternoon, and 400g of tomatoes spooned over the top is a main component, not a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is real food with fish, cheese and plenty of vegetables, and is a snack a family would happily eat again.
